title: Champions League Predictions 11/24: Perfect Real Madrid in Action, Man City Seek Response
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack7:30 PM ESTEnzo Fernández was a goalscorer on Matchday 4.  / Isaac Parkin/Manchester City FC/Getty Images We’re not quite in final stretch territory just yet, but the second half of the Champions League league phase gets underway on Tuesday evening.

Liberated by the lack of jeopardy facilitated by a bloated schedule, goals are being scored at a frighteningly entertaining rate across the continent. And while the table will start to take shape as we near the league phase’s conclusion, there’s unlikely to be any slowing down on the goalscoring front.
Real Madrid are in action on Tuesday, as are Manchester City, Arsenal and Aston Villa off the back of Premier League draws on Saturday.
So little is currently separating the best from the mediocre, and even those whose Champions League campaigns are yet to get off the ground will still feel as if time is on their side.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Tuesday’s Matchday 5 fixtures will pan out.

Back-to-back victories for LASK means their position in the league phase table is suddenly far rosier. They enter Matchday 5 above Bodø/Glimt, despite the Norwegian’s impressive home record in this competition.
A stalemate with Lille last time out means the Norwegians are now unbeaten in their previous five Champions League outings on home soil, having defeated Borussia Dortmund earlier in the campaign.

Bodø have ascended to the top of the Eliteserien since the previous matchday, beating their fellow Champions League participants and current Norwegian champions Viking 3–2 on Nov. 10. They’ve lost just one game since the start of October, but are welcoming a LASK team that may well feel it belongs on Europe’s biggest stage.
An early kick-off in Türkiye has rarely ended well for Premier League teams in recent years, with Liverpool, in particular, suffering in Istanbul.

Aston Villa are next to make the trip, and Unai Emery’s side visit Galatasaray’s daunting amphitheater off the back of a five-game winless run. The Villans passed their way to a goalless stalemate against Sunderland at the weekend, having lost at Barcelona before the break.
That was their first blemish, though, and Villa have already thrashed Gala’s eternal rivals, Fenerbahçe, 6–0 in this season’s competition, albeit on home soil.

Tuesday’s hosts have recovered from a poor start to the league phase, winning their last two, and they’ve seemingly unearthed a gem in 21-year-old Russian playmaker Aleksey Batrakov, who scored both goals in their 2–0 win over Stuttgart on Matchday 4.
Arsenal have been excellent at this stage of the competition under Mikel Arteta. /  Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: Arsenal 2–0 Borussia Dortmund

Arsenal’s world seemed to be caving in on Tyneside after such an impressive first 45 minutes, with Newcastle United overturning their halftime deficit within 17 minutes and then seeing David Raya walk off with what appeared to be a serious shoulder injury.
But the Gunners steadied themselves to earn a point, and even pulled further clear of Brighton & Hove Albion, who lost at Hull City the following day.

There appears to be no obvious contender for Arsenal’s crown domestically, and it’ll take a monster effort for any team to bypass Mikel Arteta’s stout unit at this stage of the competition. The Gunners have won 15 of their previous 16 league phase matches and are poised for another top-eight finish.
Borussia Dortmund ascended to the top of the Bundesliga table at the weekend, but their seemingly innate inferiority complex seems to often come to the fore on occasions like these.
Como produced an utterly outstanding performance on Matchday 4, becoming the first team in the Champions League era to score nine times in a single match away from home when they thumped Lens 9–1.
It was a staggering result; one indicative of the club’s meteoric rise with Cesc Fábregas at the helm. This team has no ceiling, and they’ll be expected to cruise on home soil against AEK Athens.
